name: Knight of the White Orchid
oracle_text:
First strike
When this creature enters, if an opponent controls more lands than you, you may search your library for a Plains card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.
blocked_sentences: When this creature enters, if an opponent controls more lands than you, you may search your library for a Plains card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.

needs.what: A value leaf that evaluates a count of matching objects **one player at a time** and aggregates it existentially or universally, so a condition can ask "does any single opponent control more lands than you". Concretely, the pair `{"max_count_of": {"player": "each_opponent", "objects": {"zone": "battlefield", "types": ["Land"]}}}` (the existential -- "an opponent controls more X than you") and `{"min_count_of": ...}` (the universal -- "each opponent controls more X than you" / "you control more X than each other player"), exactly mirroring the existing `min_life_of` / `max_life_of` split and for exactly the reason recorded in the comment above them in `engine/effects/values.py`. Implementation: add both names to `VALUE_KEYS`, and evaluate by running `resolve_pool` once per player returned by `select_players(ctx, spec["player"])` with the pool scoped to that one player -- the evaluator has to inject the scope itself (the way `for_each_player` injects `each_player`) rather than asking the card author for it, since a card written before the loop has no binding to name. `validate_value` needs the matching branch so a misspelling is a load error instead of a silent 0. It must be reachable from a trigger's `condition`, because the printed clause is an intervening-if (`TriggerSpec.condition`, checked in `triggers._matches` at both trigger time and resolution) and not an `if` op in the body.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `count` is the only object-counting leaf, and it resolves a single pool: `{"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "opponent", "types": ["Land"]}}` **sums across the whole table**, because `_zone_players`/`matches` treat `controller: "opponent"` as "every opponent at once". That is the printed card in a duel and a different, strictly better card at a pod. `lands_you_control` reads only your own side, so it supplies the right-hand side of the comparison and nothing else. `min_life_of`/`max_life_of` are the shape needed, but they are hard-wired to life totals. `distinct` counts distinct values over one pool, `extreme` ranks only on power/toughness/mana_value, and `exists` filters objects -- none can relate a land's controller's land count back to yours. The one per-player mechanism that does exist, `for_each_player` plus `controller: {"binding": "each_player"}`, is an **op**: it cannot appear inside a trigger's `condition` at all, and putting the test in the effects body instead would run the search once per qualifying opponent -- up to three Plains onto the battlefield at a four-player pod off a card that fetches one -- as well as dropping the on-trigger half of the intervening-if.
needs.why_it_cannot_be_approximated: Summing opponents' lands makes the gate fire in games where the printed card does nothing: at a four-player table, three opponents holding two lands each total 6 and beat your 5, so a Knight built on `count` + `controller: "opponent"` is an unconditional two-mana 2/2 that ramps, while the real card is blank when you are ahead on lands. Dropping the clause is the same card with the condition always true. Dropping the whole trigger leaves a vanilla {W}{W} 2/2 first striker whose second printed line does nothing.

notes:
Only the intervening-if blocks this card; everything else is expressible today. Once the leaf exists the ability is one triggered ability with `trigger: {"event": "self_enters", "source": "self", "condition": {"cmp": ">", "left": {"max_count_of": {"player": "each_opponent", "objects": {"zone": "battlefield", "types": ["Land"]}}}, "right": {"lands_you_control": true}}}` and a body of `may` wrapping one `search_library` with `count: 1`, `destination: "battlefield"`, `selector: {"subtypes": ["Plains"]}` -- untapped, unlike Loyal Warhound and Claim Jumper -- and no separate `shuffle` op, since `search_library` shuffles by default (`shuffles = "library" in zones and spec.get("shuffle", True)`), which is the printed "then shuffle". `subtypes` is the right filter for "a Plains card": it is an any-of subtype test, so it finds nonbasic Plains too and does not wrongly require the Basic supertype. The starting_point (2/2 Human Knight, {W}{W}, mono-white, `first_strike`) needs no change.

Sandbox note for whoever closes this: in the fixed expectation position you control 30 lands and the opponent controls 2, so the intervening-if is **false** and the search never happens. The eventual answer's expectation must therefore be `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33, "library_size": {"0": 40}, "hand_size": {"0": 0}}` -- asserting a fetched Plains (34 permanents, 39 library) would be asserting the bug. The condition and the search need an engine unit test on a board where an opponent is ahead on lands.

This capability is the grouping key for a large family already sitting in the queue with the same 'no template for' reason: Loyal Warhound, Claim Jumper, Scouting Hawk, Space Marine Scout, Beza the Bounding Spring, Aerial Surveyor, Boreas Charger, Cartographer's Hawk (all lands), plus Avatar of Might ('at least four more creatures than you' -- the same leaf with a `sum` offset on the right) and Advice from the Fae ('more creatures than each other player' -- the `min_count_of` half). Note that four of those cards are already loaded in data/cards/auto/templates.cards.json with only their keyword line implemented, and loyal_warhound additionally carries a wrong `self_enters_tapped` replacement misparsed from 'put it onto the battlefield tapped' -- worth fixing in the same pass.
